title: Upper bound of the derived tensor product of module complexes
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring and choose its derived category $D(A)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], equipped with the source K-flat derived tensor product. Let $K,L\in D(A)$ and $b,d\in\mathbf Z$. If $H^i(K)=0$ for every $i>b$ and $H^i(L)=0$ for every $i>d$, then $H^i(K\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}L)=0$ for every $i>b+d$.

source.place: DerivedCategory.isLE_tensor; ordinary-module specialization of the already proved generic source declaration; lines 441-449

proof.text: Represent K and N by good truncations zero above b and d. Replace the first truncation by its bounded-above flat resolution, still zero above b. This resolution is K-flat, so it computes the derived tensor with the second truncation. Each summand of its total tensor in degree greater than b+d is zero, because at least one factor has degree greater than its bound. Transport this strict upper bound across the two representing isomorphisms. This is the already proved source lemma isLE_tensor.
